A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lightest gauge particle in the LH model, $B_H$ can be detected at the ILC if it really exists.
, the ILC with the photon collider is the most powerful tool to probe $B_H$ in the LH model.
the LH model with $B_H$ mass of hundreds Gev can be tested at the ILC via the processes of $\gamma\gamma \to l'^+ l'^- B_{H}(l=e,\mu)$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photon collider at the ILC is a powerful probe of the new physics beyond the standard model.
the photon collider is an ideal tool to search for the new light gauge boson $ B_H $ in the LH model.
the lightest neutral gauge boson predicted by the LH model can be detected via the processes $\gamma\gamma \to f\bar fB_H$ with high confidence level at the ILC if it indeed exists.
